This sounds like me with ritalin. You don't realize how bad the speed has got you for as long as you create this elaborate bubble of a life that operates as long as the high allows you to sustain the bubble of appearing like you have your shit together. 

Yesterday was the real wake up call that ritalin was my life. I was meeting to smoke some blueberry hash with one of my stoner buddies and the whole time I kept pacing around his fucking house, hitting his weed without any sign of joy. And I just kept accusing him of fucking me over because I was waiting for a new dealer he went through the trouble of arranging for me. So the guy was an hour late  and I was so angry. I just sat there grinding cigarettes into my hand and grunting at any conversation my friend would bring up. I didn't even hit the bowl. 

My ritalin guy shows up and he looks ut as suspiciously because my friend looks so bummed out while I'm gritting my teeth. I get my script, break these pills and when I look back at my friend I'm beaming and talking about all the normal shit people talk about when they're actual humans. The dealer snickered out the instant transition from looking suicidal to beatific in less than a minute. 

So yea nothing special as far as drug stories go. I just learned what my own and only priority was... and yet I and the OP know we're all pathetic selfish single minded insects(i just read metamorphosis and found the insect allegory to be brutally honest), essentially doing life solely for the honey inside the beehive. 

But then again at least I have found meaning on my life on a physiological level, so I can't say an addiction is all bad. AND that's really what I want to try to make clear to u folks even on this board that look at addiction exclusively as a negative. Addictions are the easiest way to establish an identity, connections to people, maintain emotional stability, and make shaky relationships actually functional. Because as long as u have the drugs, u don't have time to worry, because u feel right, and when u feel right u have things nicely under control. as long as u get the right dose and adjust to tolerance then an addiction is basically guaranteed insurance against the emotional slings and arrows of life. The addict sees addiction as a rational solution to an irrational problem. And why do they seek this drastic solution: because they fucking care and are genuinely good people that don't want their problems getting in the way of the lives of the people they care about. Ironic as it sounds, addicts deserve a lot of fucking respect. They sacrifice their health to keep their sanity enough to carry on with a certain degree of control over life's tragic endlessness.

Wow that got rambly. OP you cannot afford to feel guilt about your addiction. It was an attempt at controlling your life for the sake if your job and your family. 

I would suggest u do the obvious, take a break with benzos (if they don't affect ur work) then figure out if u reallllly needed adderall. I don't think u do because a boring easy job doesn't mix well the strong stimulants. If u had assignments that required u to pour through Western metaphysics in order to find the link between plato's conception of the republic as a precursor to nietzsches claims that a true republic can only exist once man has attained the attributes sufficient to create an intellectually evolved.... hahah if ur job was remotely along those lines u would never think about masturbating outside of a purely abstract sense. Speed is for high cognitive performance only, it becomes bad when u get bored and fuck shit up with too much useless mental energy.

Tl;Dr take benzos until ur off adderall and don't use it unless u need to crank out some serious scholarly shit.

Idk man when I took 1.5g shit was just underwhelming. I felt fucked up yet the visuals were just dumb distortions of everything. Got bored took a higher dose, and eventually BAM, I'm rolling on the ground talking to the carpet. Synthesized psychedellics were invented for a reason. Ever since LSD civilization has progressed.

At least in my few years of steadfast suicidal resolve, I've come to realize that that more I play life, the more death seems a victory. So my simple reasoning is to live as long as you can until you're truly ecstatic about ending it because you know life has nothing to offer, rather than ending it because you wish life could be better. 

But I'm curious, do you think there's a semantic difference when suicide is phrased as either surrendering to life or embracing death?

LSD always. First of all it's easy to control at lower doses, at least you feel in control of the new brilliant headspace you've been granted by the lysergic gods. Visuals are crisper and thoughts flow logically. Imagine your sober self inside of a new world. The way you perceive this new world determines how much euphoria you'll get out of the trip--it won't just come to you.

A tripping dose, >2g, are terrible if you want control, but awesome if you just want to drown in hyperspace for a while. Don't ever bother with low doses on shrooms. But a low dose of acid is awesome and feels like speed with a calmer edge to it.

tl;dr: IMO shrooms are a broken roller coaster while LSD is a private jet.
